explanation.en:
後で means “after” or “later.” It is used to say that one action happens after another action or time. You can use it with verbs or nouns.

Key points:
• Verb (past short form) + 後で: 食べた後で
• Noun + の + 後で: 授業の後で
• It marks the action that happens later
• Common in daily routines

Example: “昼ご飯を食べた後で勉強します” means “I study after eating lunch.” “授業の後で友だちに会います” means “I meet my friend after class.”

When using verbs, use the past short form (た-form). When using a noun, add の before 後で.

後で can also mean “later” by itself, like “後で電話します” (I’ll call later).

Practice by describing order: 仕事の後で買い物します, 寝た後でシャワーを浴びます.

structure.pattern: (Noun + の / Verb past) + 後で + Action

examples.japanese: 昼ご飯を食べた後で勉強します。
examples.romaji: Hirugohan o tabeta ato de benkyou shimasu.

examples.japanese: 授業の後で友だちに会います。
examples.romaji: Jugyou no ato de tomodachi ni aimasu.
examples.english: I meet my friend after class.

examples.japanese: 仕事の後で買い物します。
examples.romaji: Shigoto no ato de kaimono shimasu.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using dictionary form before 後で
commonMistakes.correction: Use the past short form before 後で
commonMistakes.example: ❌ 食べる後で → ✅ 食べた後で

commonMistakes.correction: Add の before 後で with nouns
commonMistakes.example: ❌ 授業後で → ✅ 授業の後で
